page: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-32 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results place the n2-standard-32 consistently in the average performance tier across most compute and memory operations. The instance achieved a single-core stress-ng score of 1837.79 and a multi-core score of 30011.12. Memory bandwidth tests recorded 1654.01 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 166.42 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 85.05 GB/sec for large-block writes. Single-threaded gzip compression performed weakly at 23.79 GB/sec, though multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reached an average tier of 69.45 GB/sec.

The CPU supports advanced instruction sets including AVX, AVX-512, AES cryptography, and BMI2. In application-specific benchmarks, the server processed 26.98 million Redis SET operations per second and delivered a static web serving throughput of 21.35 GB/sec. For machine learning, LLM inference with a small 135M model achieved 970.58 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 81.34 tokens/sec for text generation. However, performance degrades significantly on larger models, with a 70B model prompt processing speed of 4.16 tokens/sec, indicating a clear tradeoff when running large-scale AI workloads without dedicated GPU acceleration.

Given its balanced resource allocation and mid-tier performance profile, the n2-standard-32 offers a predictable cost-to-performance ratio for standard enterprise workloads. It is suited for general-purpose applications, software compilation, database operations, and moderate web serving.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-32 is an x86_64 general-purpose server configured with 32 dedicated vCPUs and 128.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz. It lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks consistently position this instance in the average tier, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 9858.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 27193.8. The processor supports AVX-512 and AES instructions, enabling average-tier performance in cryptography and database operations. While it handles small-scale LLM inference and web serving efficiently, processing larger models reveals performance limitations. This server is best suited for balanced workloads such as software compilation, database management, and general-purpose enterprise applications.
